level_1: Elicits and reports a comprehensive history for common patient presentations, with guidance
Reconciles current data with secondary sources
level_2: Seeks data from secondary sources, with guidance
Efficiently elicits and concisely reports a patient history, incorporating pertinent psychosocial and other determinants of health
level_3: Elicits and concisely reports a hypothesis- driven patient history for common patient presentations
Uses history and secondary data to guide the need for further diagnostic testing
level_4: Independently obtains data from secondary sources
Efficiently and effectively tailors the history taking, including relevant historical subtleties, based on patient, family, and system needs
level_5: Elicits and concisely reports a hypothesis- driven patient history for complex patient presentations
Models effective use of history to guide the need for further diagnostic testing

level_1: Performs a general physical examination while attending to patient comfort and safety
Identifies and interprets uncommon and complex abnormal findings
level_2: Identifies common abnormal findings
Uses advanced maneuvers to elicit subtle findings
level_3: Performs a hypothesis- driven physical examination for a common patient presentation
Integrates subtle physical examination findings to guide diagnosis and management
level_4: Interprets common abnormal findings
Models effective evidence-based physical examination technique
level_5: Performs a hypothesis- driven physical examination for a complex patient presentation
Teaches the predictive values of the examination findings to guide diagnosis and management

level_1: Organizes and accurately summarizes information obtained from the patient evaluation to develop a clinical impression
Develops prioritized differential diagnoses in complex patient presentations and incorporates subtle, unusual, or conflicting findings
level_2: Integrates information from all sources to develop a basic differential diagnosis for common patient presentations
Continually re-appraises one’s own clinical reasoning to improve patient care in real time
level_3: Identifies clinical reasoning errors within patient care, with guidance
Coaches others to develop prioritized differential diagnoses in complex patient presentations
level_4: Develops a thorough and prioritized differential diagnosis for common patient presentations
Models how to recognize errors and reflect upon one’s own clinical reasoning
level_5: Retrospectively applies clinical reasoning principles to identify errors

level_1: Formulates management plans for common conditions, with guidance
Independently develops and implements plans to maintain and promote health, incorporating pertinent psychosocial and other determinants of health
level_2: Identifies opportunities to maintain and promote health

Uses shared decision making to develop and implement value-based (high value) comprehensive management plans for patients with comorbid and multisystem disease, including those patients requiring critical care
level_3: Develops and implements management plans for common conditions, recognizing acuity, and modifies based on the clinical course
Independently develops and implements comprehensive plans to maintain and promote health, incorporating pertinent psychosocial and other determinants of health
level_4: Develops and implements management plans to maintain and promote health, with guidance
Develops and implements comprehensive management plans for patients with rare or ambiguous presentations or unusual comorbid conditions
level_5: Develops and implements value-based (high value) management plans for patients with multisystem disease and comorbid conditions; modifies based on the clinical course

level_1: Identifies opportunities to maintain and promote health
Develops and implements management plans for common acute conditions
Develops and implements value- based (high value) comprehensive management plans for multiple chronic conditions, incorporating pertinent psychosocial and other determinants of health
level_2: Formulates management plans for a common chronic condition, with guidance
Develops and implements plans to maintain and promote health, incorporating pertinent psychosocial and other determinants of health
Develops and implements value- based (high value) management plans for patients with acute conditions
level_3: Formulates management plans for acute common conditions, with guidance
Develops and implements management plans for multiple chronic conditions
Creates and leads a comprehensive patient- centered management plan for the patient with highly complex chronic conditions, integrating recommendations from multiple disciplines
level_4: Develops and implements management plans to maintain and promote health
Develops and implements an initial management plan for patients with urgent or emergent conditions in the setting of chronic comorbidities
Develops and implements management plans for patients with subtle presentations, including rare or ambiguous conditions
level_5: Develops and implements management plans for common chronic conditions
Develops and implements value- based (high-value) comprehensive plans to maintain and promote health

level_1: Uses electronic health record (EHR) for routine patient care activities
Identifies clinical situations that can be managed through a telehealth visit
level_2: Identifies the required components for a telehealth visit
Uses EHR to facilitate achievement of quality targets for patient panels
level_3: Expands use of EHR to include and reconcile secondary data sources in patient care activities
Integrates telehealth effectively into clinical practice for the management of acute and chronic illness
level_4: Performs assigned telehealth visits using approved technology
Leads improvements to the EHR
level_5: Effectively uses EHR capabilities in managing acute and chronic care of patients
Develops and innovates new ways to use emerging technologies to augment telehealth visits

level_1: Explains the scientific knowledge (e.g., physiology, social sciences, mechanism of disease) for normal function and common medical conditions
level_2: Explains the scientific knowledge for complex medical conditions
level_3: Integrates scientific knowledge to address comorbid conditions within the context of multisystem disease
level_4: Integrates scientific knowledge to address uncommon, atypical, or complex comorbid conditions within the context of multisystem disease
level_5: Demonstrates a nuanced understanding of the scientific knowledge related to uncommon, atypical, or complex conditions

level_1: Explains the scientific basis for common therapies
level_2: Explains the indications, contraindications, risks, and benefits of common therapies
level_3: Integrates knowledge of therapeutic options in patients with comorbid conditions, multisystem disease, or uncertain diagnosis
level_4: Integrates knowledge of therapeutic options within the clinical and psychosocial context of the patient to formulate treatment options
level_5: Demonstrates a nuanced understanding of emerging, atypical, or complex therapeutic options

level_1: Explains the rationale, risks, and benefits for common diagnostic testing
Integrates complex diagnostic data accurately to reach high-probability diagnoses
level_2: Interprets results of common diagnostic tests
Integrates value and test characteristics of various diagnostic strategies in patients with comorbid conditions or multisystem disease
level_3: Explains the rationale, risks, and benefits for complex diagnostic testing
Anticipates and accounts for limitations when interpreting diagnostic data
level_4: Interprets complex diagnostic data
Demonstrates a nuanced understanding of emerging diagnostic tests and procedures
level_5: Integrates value and test characteristics of various diagnostic strategies in patients with common diseases

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events

Discloses patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Contributes to the analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
Leads teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Contributes to local quality improvement initiatives
Models the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (actual or simulated)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses sustainable quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination

Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies key components of the health care system
Engages with patients in shared decision making, informed by each patient’s payment models
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care
level_3: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how this impacts patient care
Advocates for patient care needs with consideration of the limitations of each patient’s payment model
level_4: Delivers care with consideration of each patient’s payment model
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care
level_5: Discusses how individual practice affects the regional and national health care system
Actively engaged in influencing health policy through advocacy activities at the local, regional, or national level

level_1: Demonstrates how to access, categorize, and analyze clinical evidence, with guidance
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Critically appraises and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Applies evidence, even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence, to guide care, tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence to patient care

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals

level_2: Identifies the factors that contribute to gap(s) between ideal and actual performance, with guidance

Seeks performance data consistently with adaptability, and humility
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the individualized learning plan and when necessary, improves it
level_5: Actively seeks opportunities to improve
Challenges one’s own assumptions and considers alternatives in narrowing the gap(s) between ideal and actual performance

level_1: Demonstrates professional behavior in routine situations

level_3: Demonstrates a pattern of professional behavior in complex or stressful situations

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of basic ethical principles

level_1: Performs administrative tasks and patient care responsibilities, with prompting

subcompetencies.name: Knowledge of Systemic and Individual Factors of Well-Being*

level_1: Uses language and non- verbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport
